transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I came in because... I seem to be spending far too much of my day just checking things. I keep opening the same folders, my desk drawers, and these labeled boxes I have, again and again. I just have to make sure my important papers and keepsakes are exactly where I left them. 

The frustrating part is, I'll do this even when I just checked them a few minutes before. I just can't seem to stop myself from looking.

When you feel the urge to check these items repeatedly, does it feel like an unwanted, anxiety-provoking urge you wish you could stop, or does it feel more like it's just your natural way of keeping things properly organized and correct?

It's definitely unwanted. I really wish I could stop. It doesn't feel like I'm just being organized, because... well, even when I know better, a thought will just keep needling me. 

I'll suddenly start worrying that I might have accidentally thrown away my husband's old tax papers, or... or maybe I put a family recipe in the wrong box. And I just can't seem to let it pass. If I try to ignore it, I just sit there feeling like I've done something terribly careless, and the only way to fix that feeling is to go look again.

Aside from the specific worries that make you check your papers and boxes, do you experience other unwanted, intrusive thoughts or images that pop into your mind and cause distress, even when they aren't tied to a checking urge?

No, I don't think so. Um... it really is just the papers and the keepsakes. I don't get other strange thoughts or pictures popping into my head out of nowhere. It's just that specific worry about losing something important, or... or being careless with my husband's things. Aside from that, I don't have anything else like that bothering me.
On a typical day, roughly how many hours do you spend checking these papers, drawers, or boxes in total?

Oh, I'm not entirely sure exactly how many hours it adds up to. I haven't really kept a strict clock on it. It just... it happens throughout the day. I might spend a good chunk of time in the morning, and then more later on. It definitely takes up a noticeable part of my day, but I couldn't give you a precise number of hours.
How long have you been experiencing this pattern of repeatedly checking your papers and boxes — weeks, months, or longer?
Oh, I'm not really sure exactly when it started. It's been a while, but I couldn't tell you if it's been weeks or months or... or longer. I just know it's been going on for some time now.
Would you say this checking has caused significant problems in your daily life, such as trouble getting to work on time, completing household tasks, or strain in your relationships?

Yes, it really does cause problems. Um... I've actually had to cancel my mentoring sessions, and I've been skipping my book club lately. Sometimes I just... I lose whole afternoons to all this checking. And then, well, I feel too embarrassed to have anyone come over because the apartment is still in such disarray from me going through everything. So it definitely gets in the way of my normal routine.
Aside from checking them, do you find it very difficult to throw away or get rid of papers, keepsakes, or other belongings, even ones that may not have much value?

No, I don't really have a problem with that. If something is just trash or I don't need it anymore, I can throw it away just fine. It's... well, it's really just the checking part that I get stuck on. Once I've looked at a paper and I know for sure what it is, I don't mind getting rid of it at all.
Thinking about a typical day recently, would you say the checking adds up to more than an hour in total, even if you can't give an exact count?

Yes, it definitely adds up to more than an hour. I mean, that's really why I came in to get help. I spend far too much of my day just opening the same folders, the same drawers, and those labeled boxes again and again. I just have to make sure the important papers and keepsakes are exactly where I left them. And the frustrating part is, I'll do it even when I just checked them a few minutes before. So, yes, it takes up a lot of time.
Would you say this checking behavior has been going on continuously for at least six months, or has it been shorter than that?

Well, I'm not entirely sure exactly when it started getting this bad. It feels like it's been a while, but... I couldn't say for certain if it's been a full six months. It might be shorter than that, or maybe it just crept up on me. I haven't really been keeping track of the calendar, just trying to get through the days.
Do you recognize that this checking is excessive or not really necessary, even while you feel driven to do it?

I'm not really sure how to answer that, to be honest. When I'm in the middle of doing it, it... well, it feels absolutely necessary to me. I just have this feeling that I need to be completely certain my things are safe and exactly where they belong. So I haven't really looked at it as being unnecessary, even though I know I'm spending far too much time on it. I just don't know.
Did this checking behavior start or get noticeably worse around any particular event in your life, such as your husband passing away or another significant change?

I really couldn't say. I haven't noticed it tying back to any one specific event, to be honest. I mean, even with my husband passing... I don't remember it suddenly starting or getting worse right around then. Like I mentioned, it just feels like it crept up on me over time, so I can't really pinpoint a particular change or event that set it all off. I just don't know.
